Schedule.description:
Node count over time, as a list of `[start_at, end_at)` time ranges.

Example: 5 nodes from t=0 to t=3600 is `[{"start_at": 0, "end_at": 3600, "node_count": 5}]`.

`start_at` and `end_at` must be 60-second aligned, `node_count` must be non-negative. On non-final entries, `end_at` may be omitted (inferred from the next entry's `start_at`); gaps fill with `node_count: 0`. Order and transfer times must also be on the [allocation schedule grid](https://docs.sfcompute.com/api-reference/platform/get-platform-constants#response-allocation-schedule-grid), except a start at the current time.

In responses, a non-empty array always closes with a terminator entry whose `end_at` is `null` (the unbounded tail) and, for a bounded schedule, `node_count: 0`; an empty schedule is returned as `[]`.

from_pool.description: Source pool (must belong to the authenticated caller).

instance_sku.description: Instance SKU the transfer applies to.

to_pool.description: Destination pool (must belong to the authenticated caller).

action.description: The event type. Current values are `instance.created`, `instance.running`, `instance.failed`, `instance.connection_lost`, `instance.termination_imminent`, `instance.terminated`, `order.created`, `order.filled`, `order.cancelled`, `image.published`, `image.revoked`, `image.reinstated`, `image.deprecated`, `trust_level.updated`, `instance_sku_override.updated`, and `instance_sku_override.deleted`. New values may be added later.

cursor.description: Resume the stream from just after this event by passing this value as `starting_after`.

occurred_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the event occurred.

targets.description: The resources the event is about, as `{type, id}` pairs.

v2.Limit.description: A ceiling on what your account can commit to or hold. Limits with the same `name` apply together: an account-wide row caps the total, and a row narrowed to one SKU caps that SKU within the total. Limits named `max_*` cap how many of a resource you hold at once, such as `max_instances`, and are always account-wide.

name.description: Which limit this is. The name determines the unit of `value` and `usage`.

scope.description: Where this limit applies. `{}` means it applies account-wide; `{"sku": "sku_..."}` means orders on that one SKU.

usage.description: How much of `value` your account has used, as a decimal string in the unit `name` implies (node hours, seconds, dollars, or a count). Omitted when the limit doesn't track usage or usage hasn't been measured yet.

value.description: The ceiling, as a decimal string in the unit `name` implies (node hours, seconds, dollars, or a count). `null` means unlimited.

v2.LimitScope.description: Where a limit applies. Each key names one way to narrow the limit; its value is the one thing the limit is narrowed to. A key that is absent places no restriction, so `{}` applies account-wide. Keys not listed here may appear as additional string properties when new ways to narrow a limit are added.

sku.description: The SKU this limit is narrowed to, as a `sku_...` id. Absent means the limit applies account-wide.

oneOf.description: The last event's cursor. Pass it as `starting_after` to fetch the next page. Omitted when `data` is empty.

data.description: The page of events, in the order they were recorded.

has_more.description: Whether more events are available after this page.

oneOf.description: Pass as `starting_after` or `ending_before` to paginate.

v2.OrderFill.description: A single fill event: the capacity and price this order executed at in one matching event.

allocation_schedule_delta.description: Capacity change this fill delivered. Quantities are always positive; `side` on the parent order determines whether this added or removed capacity.

v2.OrderPreviewFee.description:
Fee charged on fills for the targeted instance SKU.

Total fee = `flat_dollars_per_node_hour × node_hours` + `percentage_bps / 10000 × execution_total_dollars`, where `node_hours` is `node_count × duration_hours` for a whole-order estimate and `matched_node_minutes / 60` for a partial one.

Recomputed against the realized price at fill time.

percentage_bps.description: Percentage of execution total, in basis points (10000 = 100%).

oneOf.description: Placing this order would put the account past a limit.

name.description: The limit that would be broken.

projected_usage.description: What the account would have committed against it with this order placed.

scope.description: What that limit covers. Empty covers the whole account.

fee.description: Fee policy for the matched instance SKU.

oneOf.description: The allocation the estimate actually matched. It can be smaller than the requested schedule: an `allow_partial` estimate may match fewer nodes or less time, and an order that starts now cannot fill the minute already under way. Like the rate, it is an estimate, not a promise to fill.

matched_node_minutes.description:
Node-minutes the quoted rate was derived over, present only when the estimate matched part of the order rather than all of it. To estimate the execution total, multiply the rate by this area in node-hours (`matched_node_minutes / 60`), not by the full `allocation_schedule_delta` rectangle.

When absent, the whole order matched and the rectangle is the area to price. For a buy the product can overstate the execution total: its rate is derived over the order's remaining window less one minute, so it still clears if placement lands a minute later, and is capped at `limit_price_dollars_per_node_hour` when one is sent.

A partial quote's rate is rounded down for a sell and up for a buy, which puts the product within $0.000001 per matched node-minute of the exact total.

Treat this area as an estimate rather than a guarantee: when the match combines resting orders at different prices, posting the quoted rate as a limit may fill less than this.

notices.description: Maintenance windows for the matched instance SKU overlapping the order's delivery window.

post_order_body.description: Ready-to-submit body for `POST /v2/orders`, priced at the estimated rate. It is an estimate, not a promise to fill: the market can move before you post it, and when the match combines resting orders at different prices, posting it verbatim can fill less than estimated or nothing at all. For an `allow_partial` estimate that matched only part of the order, the price is the rate over the part that matched.

oneOf.description: Fee policy for the targeted instance SKU. Absent when no SKU could be resolved.

notices.description: Maintenance windows for the targeted instance SKU overlapping the requested order window.

reason.description: Why there is no estimate. For an `allow_partial` request, `no_availability` means no part of the order could be covered.

v2.OrderPrincipal.description: The principal that placed an order. `type` distinguishes the two cases: a user carries `email` (when an email identity exists); a token carries `name`. The inapplicable field is omitted.

email.description: Email of the user, when the principal is a user with a recorded email.

id.description: `users.id` for a user principal, `api_tokens.id` for a token principal.

name.description: Name of the API token, when the principal is a token.

v2.OrderPrincipalKind.description: Whether an order's `created_by` principal is a human user or an API token.

allocation_schedule_delta.description: Change in capacity if the order fills. Must be a single time range with both `start_at` and `end_at`.

allow_partial.description: If true, the order may fill partially — fewer nodes and/or a subset of the requested time window.

allow_standing.description: If true, the order stays in the order book until either fills, is explicitly cancelled, or the order end time is reached resulting in automatic cancellation. If false, the order is cancelled immediately if it doesn't fill.

capacity.description: Deprecated — use `pool`. Target pool that receives or loses compute if this order fills (depending on order type).

oneOf.description: Principal that placed the order — the human user when known, otherwise the API token that placed it. `null` for orders that predate attribution. Always present (value-or-null) like other order attributes, since every order conceptually has a creator.

filled_allocation_schedule_delta.description: The total portion of the requested schedule that has filled. Once `status` is `cancelled`, this is final and remains available on later get and list responses. Empty for orders with no fills; the unfilled remainder is `allocation_schedule_delta` minus this.

fills.description: Complete list of fills produced by this order. Once `status` is `cancelled`, this list is final and remains available on later get and list responses. Omitted for orders with no fills.

instance_sku.description: Instance SKU this order is pinned to. Carries the SKU's human-readable name when one is registered.

v2.PatchPoolRequest.description: Update a pool. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

oneOf.description: Metadata tags. Full replacement semantics: replaces all existing tags. Omit to leave tags unchanged. Set to `null` to clear all tags.

v2.PoolKind.description:
Pool kind determines what operations are allowed on a pool.

- `Market`: User-created pools. - `Originating`: Provider pools for selling compute. Cannot add compute   (buy orders/procurements). - `ReadOnly`: System-managed pools used for legacy compute, bare metal   contracts, and other. Cannot be modified through the API.

v2.PoolTransferResponsePreview.description: A transfer of compute from one pool (`from_pool`) to another (`to_pool`).

allocation_schedule_delta.description: The transfer's allocation schedule, expanded into constant-quantity rectangles. The final rectangle has `end_at: null` (the unbounded tail); gaps are represented as explicit zero-quantity rectangles.

instance_sku.description: Instance SKU the transfer applied to. Carries the SKU's human-readable name when one is registered.

rejected_reason.description: Reason a pool transfer was rejected.

v2.PoolTransferStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a pool transfer.

allow_partial.description: If true, the estimate models an order that may fill partially — fewer nodes and/or a subset of the requested time window — instead of one that fills completely or not at all. Send the same value you will send as `allow_partial` on `POST /v2/orders`, or the estimate answers for a different order than the one you place. Absent means all-or-nothing.

duration_seconds.description: Order duration in seconds, a multiple of 60. The order must end on the [allocation schedule grid](https://docs.sfcompute.com/api-reference/platform/get-platform-constants#response-allocation-schedule-grid).

oneOf.description: The least you will accept. The estimate models a sell limited to this rate instead of one that takes any price, so it answers what an order at this limit would fill: the matched part's average rate stays at or over it, and when nothing can match within it, the response is `unavailable` with reason `no_availability`. The quoted rate is never below this value. Absent means any price.

node_count.description: Number of nodes. Must be positive.

oneOf.description: Pool the order draws from. Omit to get an estimate without pinning to a pool. The response body then returns a placeholder you must replace before submitting to `/v2/orders`.

start_at.description: Order start: a time on the [allocation schedule grid](https://docs.sfcompute.com/api-reference/platform/get-platform-constants#response-allocation-schedule-grid), or the current time.
